title: The power of the powerless
text: From France to Chile, Serbia to Indonesia, citizens who feel they have no control over the institutions that shape their lives are protesting. Political scientist John Keane calls these revolts of the powerless: the powerful always depend on the cooperation of the many, and power is exposed as contingent the moment the powerless refuse to cooperate. He suggests these may be slow-motion democratic revolutions rather than passing outrages.
use: For 'When two elephants fight, it is the grass that gets trampled' (2026) and 'Nearly all men can stand adversity, but to test the character, give him power' (2024).

title: Running in a saree
text: In Ramgarh, Jharkhand, about 6,000 women ran trial races for a few Home Guard posts; some in shorts changed at the stadium because they cannot wear them in the village, others ran in sarees. Meena Kumari, 24, who left college when her parents could not afford it, said people will talk behind her back, but one day they will praise her.
use: For 'Girls are weighed down by restrictions, boys with demands' (2023), 'If development is not engendered, it is endangered' (2016) and 'Hand that rocks the cradle rules the world' (2021).

title: Due process for the despised
text: The film Prahaar revisits the 26/11 trial: why should a man who attacked innocents get a trial at all? Its answer is that the law must hold even when public anger demands otherwise, and that a democracy is tested by how it protects those it despises. Kasab's defence lawyer was branded a 'terrorist lawyer' simply for doing his job.
use: For 'A society that has more justice is a society that needs less charity' (2023) and 'Truth knows no colour' (2025).

title: Poverty halved, earnings flat
text: The World Bank says extreme poverty fell from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023, lifting about 496 million people above the $4.2 line. Yet real earnings stayed broadly flat, the top 10% of workers earn about 13 times the bottom 10%, and 57% of the poor live in one belt from UP to West Bengal.
use: For 'There can be no social justice without economic prosperity, but economic prosperity without social justice is meaningless' (2020) and 'Poverty anywhere is a threat to prosperity everywhere' (2018).

title: Serbia: from a canopy collapse to a change of government
text: In November 2024 a canopy collapsed at Novi Sad railway station in Serbia, killing 16. It became a symbol of alleged corruption and lack of accountability. Students began with campus assemblies and blockades; teachers, farmers and actors joined. In two years their 'Student List' won 141 of 250 seats, peacefully unseating President Vučić after over a decade in power.
use: For 'With greater power comes greater responsibility' (2014) and 'Nearly all men can stand adversity, but to test the character, give him power' (2024).

title: Millionaires without a middle class
text: India has 9.4 lakh dollar millionaires (UBS) and may soon have a million, yet 43% of its workers are still in agriculture and 79% of non-farm workers are in informal firms. It is producing rich people faster than a broad middle class.
use: For 'There can be no social justice without economic prosperity but economic prosperity without social justice is meaningless' (2020).

title: 'An economy of care, experience and intergenerational solidarity'
text: Keralam, where the elderly may be 30% of the people by 2051, is urged to turn ageing into a silver economy: care jobs for the young, mentoring by retired teachers and nurses, and dignity for the old.
use: For journey and justice essays: 'The years teach much which the days never know', 'Life is a long journey between human being and being humane'.

title: More complex than black and white squares
text: Opening anecdote: In October 2026, FIDE, the world chess body, published its first survey of women players. The findings were far more complex than the black-and-white squares of the board: 76% of 672 women from 127 countries reported discrimination or harassment, 63% faced gender bias in chess settings, and 38% faced sexual harassment. India sent the most respondents.
use: Open a gender essay with it, then widen to sport, work and society: 'Patriarchy is the least noticed yet the most significant structure of social inequality', 'Girls are weighed down by restrictions, boys with demands'.

title: The girl whose questions outran her teachers
text: Diksha Nagarkoti grew up in Pithoragarh, on the Indo-Nepal border, watching the mountains change with the seasons and wondering how ecosystems worked. Her teachers could not answer all her questions. She found her answers through VigyanShaala's STEM mentors; over 20,000 young women, most of them first-generation learners, have joined its She for STEM programme.
use: Open or illustrate: 'A well-educated mind will always have more questions than answers' (2026), 'The Empires of the future will be the empires of the mind' (2024).

title: Nepal and the first loss-and-damage grant
text: Nepal accounts for barely 0.1% of global emissions, yet floods triggered by an ice-and-rock avalanche claimed more than 1,400 lives and destroyed at least 10% of its hydropower facilities. Developed countries agreed to the grant only after insisting it be treated as an exception, not a precedent.
use: Our suggested link: a contemporary illustration of 'When two elephants fight, it is the grass that gets trampled', and of justice versus charity (compensation, not aid).

title: FIDE's first survey of women in chess
text: 76% of 672 female respondents from 127 federations reported discrimination or harassment. 44% considered stepping away from chess, and 54% never had a female role model or mentor. India was the largest contributor, with 69 respondents.
use: Fresh data for gender-justice essays ('Patriarchy is the least noticed yet most significant structure...'). The lack of mentors shows 'restrictions' at work.

title: Ageing with dignity: Keralam's elder-rights law
text: Keralam's new law gives senior citizens the right to age at home, recognises living wills, and regulates care homes and caregivers. The Chief Minister called it a realisation that 'our world is changing'.
use: For 'Life is a long journey between human being and being humane', 'The years teach much...' and 'Hand that rocks the cradle' (care work).
